rationale: This is effectively an intangible-capital-adjusted inverse-leverage measure (known R&D-capital/low-leverage territory) and is substantively the same economic construct as the archive's already-tested "Organic R&D Liability Coverage," with the added problem that the raw unranked ratio explodes for low-liability firms.

It is the archive's "Post-Acquisition Debt Cleanup" with a gross-margin term bolted on via SUMRANK — a cosmetic augmentation that also dilutes the goodwill-decline leg, and the closely analogous "Debt-Retirement R&D Margin Confirmation" already failed.

Multiplying two same-signed rank legs (debt growth and intangible-asset growth) yields a signal dominated by the well-known asset-growth/debt-issuance main effects rather than a true conditional interaction, and it overlaps the archive's rollover/intangible-build family.

The R&D-retrenchment × liability-growth interaction is already tested in the archive, and the only new element — adding dividend intensity positively inside the "bad financing" leg — is internally inconsistent since high payout is normally associated with higher, not lower, expected returns.

Substantively a rediscovery of the archive's "Liability Growth R&D Retrenchment" (and of the standalone net-external-financing anomaly), with only the leverage-flow proxy and the addition of advertising to the intangible leg changed.

The gross-margin conditioner is a defensible economic addition, but the construction is a variant of the archive's strong "Organic R&D Liability Coverage" and is numerically fragile: an unranked triple ratio whose sign flips with negative gross margins and whose magnitude explodes as lt/at approaches zero.
